newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Elder statesmen urge end to Ecuadorean crisis.
newsitem.headline: Elder statesmen urge end to Ecuadorean crisis.

text.p: Two of Ecuador's elder statesmen publicly endorsed calls by leading newspapers on Saturday for all three of the country's current "presidents" to resign.

El Comercio of Quito and El Universo of Guayaquil both said the constitutional crisis -- prompted by the fact that three people were simultaneously claiming to be president -- had created a power vacuum that could only lead to political bloodletting or a military dictatorship.
Former presidents Osvaldo Hurtado and Sixto Duran Ballen issued a joint statement effectively urging the three claimants to Ecuador's presidential throne to step aside for the good of their country.
"We wish to express our agreement with the proposal of the forementioned newspapers. We invite all social sectors to support it and the National Congress to embrace it," the ex-presidents said.
Abdala Bucaram was voted out of office by a divided Congress on Thursday on grounds of mental incompetence.

He has dismissed the vote as an attempted coup, however, and said he has no intention of handing over power to Fabian Alarcon, the congressional leader appointed interim head of state by his fellow lawmakers Thursday night.

Bucaram, whose hold on power looked increasingly shaky Saturday, has also indicated that he would not be willing to hand power to Vice President Rosalia Arteaga, who claims she is his only legal successor.
